dishes.title: Mille-Feuille
dishes.summary: Rough puff pastry made in four turns, baked flat under a weighted tray so it rises in crisp, even sheets, layered with vanilla crème pâtissière and finished with a fondant glaze feathered with chocolate, then cut into clean slices. It closes the Sous Chef desserts as the pastry kitchen's showpiece: lamination, custard, glazing and a clean cut in one plate.
skills: puff pastry baked flat under a tray
equipment: Mixing bowl and a bench scraper
Rolling pin and a ruler
Two flat baking trays of the same size, and two sheets of baking paper
Something heavy and ovenproof to weigh the top tray, such as an ovenproof dish
Instant read thermometer
Medium saucepan, whisk and fine sieve for the pastry cream
Piping bag with a plain 1/2 inch (1.2 cm) nozzle
Small paper piping cone or a sandwich bag for the chocolate
Offset palette knife and a cocktail stick
Long serrated knife and a long sharp knife

ingredients.item: Cold unsalted butter, in 3/4 inch (2 cm) cubes
Icing sugar, for caramelising the pastry
Whole milk, for the pastry cream
Vanilla pod, split, or vanilla bean paste
Unsalted butter, for the pastry cream
Water or milk, for the glaze
Golden syrup or light corn syrup

mise: Rough puff: toss the butter cubes through the flour and salt, pressing each cube flat once between finger and thumb, stopping while the pieces are thumbnail size. Add the iced water and lemon juice and bring together with the scraper into a shaggy, marbled block. Wrap and chill 20 minutes.

Pastry cream: make it as in the Boston cream pie, with the quantities here: heat the milk with the vanilla; whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour; temper; return to the pan and boil 1 full minute, whisking; beat in the butter; sieve; press film on the surface and chill at least 2 hours.
Check the dough temperature with the thermometer before each roll: it should be 54 to 59°F (12 to 15°C).
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) when the pastry has had its final rest.

timeline.do: Make the rough puff block; chill 20 minutes; make the pastry cream and chill.
Four letter turns with rests between.
Roll to a thin sheet; prick; chill 30 minutes; oven on.
Bake weighted 20 minutes, then 10 to 15 minutes uncovered; caramelise; cool.
Trim and cut into three strips; glaze and feather the top strip.
Pipe the cream and assemble; chill 30 minutes; cut and serve.

steps.do: Turns: on a lightly floured worktop, roll the block into a rectangle three times as long as it is wide, about 15 by 5 inches (38 by 13 cm). Fold the bottom third up and the top third down like a letter, turn 90 degrees and repeat. Wrap and chill 30 minutes. Give two more letter turns the same way, then chill 30 minutes.
steps.look: The shaggy block becomes a smooth dough with streaks of butter visible; the edges stay straight.
steps.mistake: Rolling when the dough is warm, so butter smears through the surface and the layers fuse.
steps.fix: If butter breaks through or the dough feels soft, chill 20 minutes before carrying on; flour any butter that shows.

steps.do: Roll the dough into a thin rectangle about 13 by 10 inches (33 by 25 cm), a scant 1/8 inch (3 mm) thick. Lay it on a baking paper lined tray, prick it all over with a fork every 1/2 inch (1 cm) and chill 30 minutes.
steps.look: An even, thin sheet covered in small holes.
steps.mistake: Skipping the pricking and resting, so the pastry shrinks and rises unevenly.
steps.fix: Prick thoroughly and rest cold; a rested sheet bakes flat and even.

steps.do: Cover the pastry with a second sheet of baking paper and the second tray, then put a heavy ovenproof dish on top. Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes. Remove the weight, top tray and paper and bake 10 to 15 minutes more until deep golden and crisp all through.
steps.look: A flat, even, deep golden sheet with tightly packed, crisp layers visible at the edges.
steps.mistake: Taking it out pale, so the inner layers are doughy and turn soggy under the cream.
steps.fix: Bake until deep golden; break off a corner: it should be crisp right through.

steps.do: Optional: raise the oven to 450°F (230°C), dust the pastry with the 2 tbsp (16 g) icing sugar and bake 2 to 4 minutes until the sugar melts into a shiny glaze. Watch closely. Cool completely on a rack.
steps.look: A thin, glossy caramel sheen over the pastry.
steps.mistake: Walking away, so the sugar burns black in seconds.
steps.fix: Stay at the oven and pull it as soon as it shines.

steps.do: Trim the edges of the cooled pastry with the serrated knife using a gentle sawing motion, then cut it lengthwise into three equal strips about 3 inches (7.5 cm) wide and 12 inches (30 cm) long. Choose the flattest strip for the top.
steps.look: Three straight, even strips with clean edges.
steps.mistake: Pressing down hard with a knife, which shatters the pastry.
steps.fix: Saw gently and let the knife do the work.

steps.do: Glaze: mix the icing sugar, syrup and water a little at a time until thick but spreadable. Spread over the top strip with the palette knife in a thin, even layer. Immediately pipe thin lines of melted chocolate across it about 1/2 inch (1 cm) apart, then drag a cocktail stick through the lines lengthwise, alternating direction every 1 inch (2.5 cm), to feather them. Leave to set 20 minutes.
steps.look: A glossy white glaze with a neat chevron or feather pattern of dark chocolate.
steps.mistake: Waiting before feathering, so the glaze sets and the pattern drags in clumps.
steps.fix: Pipe and feather immediately while the glaze is still wet; make the glaze thicker if it runs off the edges.

steps.do: Whisk the chilled pastry cream briefly until smooth and put it in the piping bag. Pipe neat rows of cream in small bulbs or lines over the first strip, about 3/4 inch (2 cm) thick. Lay the second strip on top and press gently, pipe a second layer of cream, then set the glazed strip on top. Chill 30 minutes.
steps.look: A neat, straight stack with even layers of cream visible at the sides.
steps.mistake: Spreading soft cream with a knife, which squeezes out and looks untidy.
steps.fix: Pipe with chilled, thick cream; neaten the sides with a palette knife.

steps.do: Cut into 4 slices about 3 inches (7.5 cm) wide: first score through the glaze and top layer with the serrated knife, then cut down through the rest in one firm push with the long sharp knife, wiping it between cuts.
steps.look: Clean slices showing three crisp pastry layers and two layers of cream, the feathered glaze intact.
steps.mistake: Pressing straight down through all the layers at once, which squeezes the cream out.
steps.fix: Saw gently through the top layer first, then press through the rest; some cooks cut the glazed top strip into portions before stacking.

dishes.science: Rough puff layers form when lumps of cold butter are rolled and folded into thin sheets between layers of dough. Each letter fold triples the number of layers, so four folds give 81 layers of butter. Butter is about 16 to 18 percent water; in the oven that water turns to steam and lifts the dough layers apart, while the fat keeps them separate and fries them crisp. Butter is plastic between about 59 and 66°F (15 and 19°C); colder it shatters, warmer it melts into the flour. A weighted tray stops the pastry rising tall and unevenly, so it bakes into thin, dense, crisp sheets that can hold cream. The pastry cream boils so its starch is fully swollen and the yolk enzyme that would thin it is destroyed.
dishes.plating: Lay a slice flat in the centre of a long rectangular or white plate, with the feathered glaze facing up and the cut side towards the guest so all the layers show. Add a few fresh raspberries or a small spoon of berry coulis at one side. Serve within an hour of assembly, while the pastry is still crisp, with a dessert fork and knife.

pairing.drink: A great Sauternes or a demi sec Champagne: honeyed sweetness and acidity for buttery pastry and vanilla cream, a fitting close.
pairing.brennans: Château d’Yquem Sauternes 2015 (375 ml): a half bottle of the most famous Sauternes from the Brennan's list, a showpiece wine for the showpiece of the pastry kitchen.

variations: Berry mille-feuille: lay sliced strawberries or raspberries between the bulbs of cream in each layer.
Chocolate: fold 2 oz (55 g) melted dark chocolate into the warm pastry cream.
Shop puff pastry: use a 11 oz (320 g) all butter sheet, baked weighted the same way, when time is short.
safety: The pastry cream boils for a full minute, so its eggs are fully cooked; keep the assembled mille-feuille refrigerated and eat within 1 day.
Caramelising sugar at 450°F (230°C) burns quickly and the tray is very hot; use oven gloves.
